subject: Cloud Computing
title: Azure's Government Cloud
description: A micro-lesson that makes Azure's Government Cloud usable.

hook.text: The U.S. Department of Defense wanted a $10 billion cloud contract. Microsoft won it — then lost it — then won again.

buildup.text: JEDI, the Pentagon's cloud deal, was designed as winner-take-all. Microsoft beat AWS in the final round.

discovery.text: Azure Government runs in isolated data centers with special security clearances required for access.

twist.text: AWS protested, claiming political bias. The contract was eventually canceled and replaced with a multi-cloud deal.

climax.text: Government cloud is a massive market. Azure's security certifications give it a strong advantage.

punchline.text: Government cloud contracts are worth billions. And lawsuits.

quiz.question: What happened to the JEDI cloud contract?
options: Microsoft won, AWS protested, and the contract was eventually canceled and restructured
AWS won the contract and completed it without issues
Google Cloud won and built the Pentagon's entire infrastructure

details.summary: Azure Government provides dedicated cloud regions for US government agencies meeting FedRAMP High, DoD IL5, and other compliance requirements. Operated by screened US citizens and physically separated from commercial Azure, it serves defense, intelligence, and civilian agencies.
details.whyItMatters: Government cloud contracts are worth billions and demonstrate the highest levels of trust in cloud security. Azure's government cloud presence strengthens its enterprise credibility across all sectors.
takeaways: Azure Government runs in physically separate US data centers
It meets FedRAMP High, DoD, and intelligence community standards
Only screened US citizens operate government cloud regions

faq.question: How does Azure Government differ from commercial Azure?
faq.answer: Azure Government runs in dedicated data centers isolated from commercial infrastructure. It is operated exclusively by screened US personnel. It supports higher compliance levels including DoD Impact Level 5 and Secret regions for classified workloads.

faq.question: Why is government cloud important for Microsoft?
faq.answer: Government cloud contracts provide large, stable revenue and validate Azure's security capabilities. The $10 billion JEDI contract, later replaced by JWCC, demonstrated the scale of government cloud spending. Government adoption also reassures commercial enterprises about security.
